blurb: Built by an unknown architect in 1828 for William Jenkins, lawyer and bank president, Wheatland consisted of a mansion and several outbuildings on 156.5 acres of land. The mansion itself was built in the Federal Style of the period, which highlighted symmetry and Greek Revival architecture. The construction is split into three parts that include a center section and two wings on either side.
